content:
The image shows a soybean stem with pink/purple discoloration along its length, with small reddish lesions/spots visible on the stem. The leaves in the background appear mostly healthy and green.

Key observations:
- The stem shows a distinct pinkish-purple discoloration covering a large section
- Small reddish-brown lesions/spots are visible along the stem
- The stem tissue appears affected but not completely necrotic
- No white mold, no sclerotia, no water-soaking visible
- Leaves appear relatively healthy

Matching against the symptom descriptions:

- **Anthracnose**: Red to brown dark irregular lesions on stems with black acervuli — the reddish lesions fit somewhat, but no visible black fruiting bodies
- **Cercospora**: Purple/bronze discoloration — primarily a leaf disease
- **Purple_Seed_Stain**: "sunken red lesions on petioles and stems up to 1/4 inch long" with "reddish-purple bronzing" — the pink/purple stem discoloration and small reddish spots on the stem fit this description well
- **Stem_Canker**: Dark brown to black cankers — color doesn't match; the stem here is pink/light purple, not dark brown/black

The pink-to-purple stem discoloration with small reddish lesions on the stem strongly matches **Purple_Seed_Stain** (caused by *Cercospora kikuchii*), which is known to cause "sunken red lesions on petioles and stems" and "reddish-purple bronzing" on stems and petioles in addition to the seed symptoms.
